mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the median rank IC over triggered windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to produce a statistically significant negative mean return at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered windows (p > 0.10 in two-tailed t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism's predictive power decays to non-significance in rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 3% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index above 3% for three months signals a breakdown in the inflation-fighting credibility of the central bank, which increases uncertainty and volatility, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors seek risk assets.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered windows, or the mechanism fails to activate more than once per 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns regardless of the economic cycle.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of strong payroll growth, or the mechanism's hit rate falls below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 2% month-over-month indicates a strong demand rebound after a prior contraction, which lifts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 mom > 2% AND HOUST mom > 2% after two prior months of contraction
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered recoveries, or the mechanism activates in fewer than 40% of eligible post-contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered manufacturing expansions, or the mechanism fails to activate in more than 30% of eligible periods.
